title: The Truth About Mother
next_chapter_hook: Just as Chen Ji was processing the truth about his mother, an urgent warning rang out from the depths of the Tianji Record—someone had found the entrance.

text.content: The sigh pierced through ten thousand years, carrying sealed memories that crashed into Chen Ji's Mental Sea. His body froze, the Tianji Record Fragment in his hand trembled violently, golden runes scattering like startled fireflies. 'Impossible...' he murmured, his voice hoarse and unfamiliar even to himself. That voice was too familiar, familiar enough to create the first crack in the wall of cold indifference he'd built over seventeen years. Mother, she had clearly... when Chen Ji was seven...

The Tianji Record flipped pages automatically, golden text reorganizing itself like living creatures in the void. A hazy figure slowly coalesced within the light. Chen Ji stared fixedly at that silhouette, his pupils contracting—that was a face he'd traced countless times in his midnight dreams, gentle brows and eyes, but with an expression of resolve he'd never seen before. 'Ji'er...' the voice wailed, 'Mother has waited for this day, for so very long.'

dialogue.content: 'You're not Mother.' Chen Ji's voice turned cold as a blade tempered in ice, 'I watched her take her last breath with my own eyes, buried her with my own hands. No one can deceive me—unless, it's a dead person.' He stared at the phantom, emotions churning like monstrous waves in his eyes, 'What exactly are you? Why impersonate her?'

text.content: The phantom shook her head gently, a bitter smile appearing in her eyes. 'Foolish child, Mother never left you.' Her voice carried endless exhaustion, 'The death you witnessed was merely a cicada shedding its skin that evaded the eyes of Heaven. That fire at Chen Village... I orchestrated it myself, to completely remove you from the sight of this chess game.' The Tianji Record's runes suddenly blazed brightly, countless scenes flickering like a whirling lantern—a woman's silhouette standing alone in the night, facing heavenly tribulation lightning.

dialogue.content: 'For me?' Chen Ji abruptly raised his head, his voice rising sharply, 'Do you have any idea what these years have been like for me? Called a jinx by the whole village, treated like a dog by Tianqing Sect, every time I was stomped into the mud I thought—if only you were here!' He gripped the Tianji Record tightly, his knuckles white, 'Now you're telling me this was all for me?'

text.content: The phantom fell silent for a moment, then spoke slowly: 'Ji'er, do you know Mother's true identity?' She waved her hand, and a brilliant river of stars spread across the void. Chen Ji saw a blurry female figure standing at the end of the star river, surrounded by profound laws he'd never witnessed. 'Ten thousand years ago, the Eye of Heaven schemed across the world, wanting to refine all seers into nourishment. And I... was the piece it chose but which betrayed it.' Her voice carried ten thousand years of vicissitudes, 'The true master of the Tianji Record was never just Chen Xuan alone.'

Chen Ji's pupils shook violently, as if thunder was exploding in his Mental Sea. 'Are you saying... the Tianji Record has two masters?' He stared fixedly at the phantom, countless thoughts colliding madly. Mother had always accompanied him growing up with a mortal body, he'd witnessed every morning she spent washing, sewing, bustling at the stove—if that was all fake, then everything in his memories... 'No.' He stepped back sharply, 'You're lying to me.'

The phantom made no rebuttal, simply watching him quietly. 'The Tianji Record requires three verifications to acknowledge a master—bloodline, talent, and fate.' Her voice was like a still ancient well, 'Chen Xuan passed the first two, but failed at the fate verification. And you... Ji'er, from the moment you were born, your fate was perfectly aligned with the Tianji Record.' She gazed into some distant point in the void, as if observing something, 'This was no accident—it is a path I paved for you through ten thousand years of careful arrangement.'

dialogue.content: 'Ten thousand years of arrangement?' Chen Ji laughed coldly, but the笑意 didn't reach his eyes, 'So I was your chess piece from the very beginning? The wailing baby in swaddling clothes, the confused child who buried you at seven, the useless dog现在的丧家之犬在天青宗——这一切都在你计算之中？'他的声音渐渐低沉，却更加冰冷，'那我倒想知道，娘亲——或者说，前辈——你布局万年的真正目的是什么？'

choice.prompt: 面对母亲的真相，陈机内心翻涌着震惊与愤怒，但他的第一反应是什么？

choices.description: 压下心中翻涌的情绪，以最冷静的姿态逼问母亲完整的计划
choices.risk_hint: 可能触碰到更深的秘密

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, forcibly pressing the churning emotions into the deepest part of his heart. When he spoke again, his voice had become terrifyingly calm: 'Fine. Since you've arranged this for ten thousand years, then please, Mother, explain clearly—what exactly is the Eye of Heaven? What role do I play in your chess game?' His gaze was as deep as an ancient well, as if looking at a stranger.

The phantom nodded slightly, a flicker of relief passing through her eyes: 'Worthy of being my son, even upon learning the truth you remain so composed.' She waved her hand again, and a massive chessboard phantom appeared in the star river, countless points of light arranged upon it like chess pieces. 'The Eye of Heaven is an existence that transcends this realm. It views all seers as prey, and the Tianji Record... is merely one of its numerous traps.'

choices.description: 直接表达被操控的愤怒，质问母亲凭什么替他做决定
choices.risk_hint: 可能影响后续信息获取

text.content: 'Enough!' Chen Ji abruptly interrupted, the phantom trembling slightly from the force. 'You think giving me some lofty mission will make me grateful?' He spoke word by word, 'Where were you when I waited at the village gate at seven for someone to claim my body? Where were you when Tianqing Sect's servants trampled my face and asked if I wanted to lick their shoes?' His voice turned hoarse, 'I don't need your chess game, I just need a mother.'

dialogue.content: The phantom's silhouette trembled violently, and tears finally appeared in those eyes so identical to Chen Ji's. "Ji'er... I'm sorry." Her voice broke. "How could Mother not want to watch you grow up? But the Heavenly Eye is everywhere—if I stayed, you wouldn't survive past three." She closed her eyes. "Every time I watched you being bullied from afar, my heart felt like it was being sliced, yet I could only... grit my teeth and walk away."

choices.description: Examining the mother from a strategist's perspective, suspecting ulterior motives
choices.risk_hint: Possibly misunderstanding the mother's true heart

text.content: Chen Ji slowly closed his eyes, and when he opened them again, there was not a trace of emotion in them. "Brilliant." He clapped softly. "Ten thousand years of scheming, self-sacrifice, the loving mother act—if this script were spread abroad, even the Heavenly Eye would applaud you." He tilted his head, his tone playful. "But there's one thing this junior doesn't understand—you keep saying it's for my own good, yet aren't those five characters 'it's for your own good' the greatest lie in this world?"

dialogue.content: "Do you think I would believe a woman who even acts out her death?" Chen Ji stared at the phantom, a cold sneer on his lips. "Speak—what do you truly want? To use my hand against the Heavenly Eye, or are you and it in this together?" His voice froze like winter ice. "Don't disappoint me, Mother. After all, you taught me everything."

text.content: The phantom fell silent for so long that Chen Ji thought she would never speak again. "You've truly grown up." she finally said, her voice filled with complex emotions. "Suspicious, cautious, calculating everything—these are all qualities I deliberately cultivated. But seeing you become like this, Mother doesn't know whether to feel proud or heartbroken." She waved her hand, and on the phantom chessboard, a blurry outline appeared—a man bearing seven-tenths resemblance to Chen Ji, confronting a massive eye.

"That man was Chen Xuan." Chen Xuan was my junior fellow," the phantom's voice was terrifyingly calm. "Ten thousand years ago, we were both chosen by the Heavenly Eye to become pieces. But Chen Xuan chose to fight to the end, while I... chose another path." She paused. "Lurking, scheming, waiting for the right moment. For ten thousand years, I watched him fail again and again, watched the Heavenly Eye crush him, yet he still left the seeds of the Tianji Record in the ruins." Her gaze fell on Chen Ji. "And you, Ji'er, are the sprout from that seed breaking through the soil."

dialogue.content: Chen Ji silently digested this flood of information. He recalled what Mo Xiansheng had once said—that the Tianji Record's inheritance had never been broken. So that was it—the inheritance wasn't about the technique, but about a plan spanning ten thousand years. "So Elder Chen Xuan's remnant soul..." he began, his voice somewhat hoarse, "Did he know you were still 'alive'?" The phantom shook her head with a bitter smile: "He believed I was dead until his final moment. I deceived everyone, including him. This is the most basic quality of a chess player—never let anyone know all your cards."

text.content: Chen Ji suddenly laughed, his laughter hollow and sharp. "What a chess player indeed." He stared at the phantom. "Then permit this junior to ask—how many moves have you made in this ten-thousand-year chess game? What's the score?" The phantom didn't avoid his gaze: "The Heavenly Eye has been scheming for a hundred thousand years, while I've schemed for ten thousand. Currently... I've lost nine-tenths of it." Chen Ji's pupils contracted. "However," she turned the conversation, "it made a fatal mistake—it shouldn't have let you obtain the Tianji Record while alive."

The Tianji Record suddenly quivered violently, and the phantom's form began to blur. "Time is running out." Her voice became urgent. "Ji'er, Mother's remnant soul can't hold much longer. What I say next, you must remember—the Heavenly Eye chose the seers because there's something in their bodies that it needs: the Heavenly Fate Axis. And the Heavenly Fate Axis in your body... is the purest thread in ten thousand years." She reached up, as if to touch Chen Ji's face, but passed through his body.

dialogue.content: "So I was a sacrifice from the start?" Chen Ji's voice held no inflection, as if stating an unimportant fact. The phantom shook her head, her eyes full of heartache: "No, you're not a sacrifice—you're the key to breaking the game. Your Heavenly Fate Axis is so pure that it can devour the Heavenly Eye in reverse—something it never imagined." She took a deep breath. "So I need you to do one thing: live, grow stronger, then... go to the core of the Heavenly Eye and destroy it completely."

choice.prompt: Mother's commission forces Chen Ji to face a choice—is this task a chess game that began ten thousand years ago, or her true wish?

choices.description: Since we must destroy the Heavenly Eye, we first need to know where it is
choices.risk_hint: The remnant soul may dissipate at any moment

text.content: "The core location?" Chen Ji seized on the keyword. "Where?" The phantom's form grew ever fainter, and she urgently said: "The core of the Heavenly Eye is—" Before she could finish, she suddenly clutched her chest, her form twisting violently. "Damn it, the Heavenly Eye has sensed my aura, it's—" Her voice came in fragments. "Ancient Forbidden Land... your sister... Chen Nian..."

Chen Ji shuddered all over. His sister! The Heavenly Fate Lock that the Holy Sect took away! "What happened to Chen Nian?" He grabbed toward the phantom, but only caught emptiness. The phantom struggled to speak: "She's... another trump card I left behind... You're not alone, Ji'er... Find her... You two..." The phantom suddenly exploded into countless specks of light, the Tianji Record let out a sharp mournful cry, and automatically closed that page.

choices.description: Chen Nian was taken by the Holy Sect ten thousand years later, so how could Mother have left a trump card about her?
choices.visible_cost: May cause the remnant soul to dissipate faster
choices.visible_reward: Unraveling the Mystery of My Sister's Origins
choices.risk_hint: The remnant soul might dissipate prematurely

text.content: "Wait!" Chen Ji shouted sharply, interrupting, "You said Chen Nian is a piece you left behind? But she was clearly taken by the Holy Sect—" He suddenly realized something, his pupils contracting, "The Holy Sect capturing her was also part of your plan?" The phantom's figure trembled violently, as if enduring unbearable agony: "Ji'er... Chen Nian is... not just your sister... She is another chess piece I "borrowed" from the river of time at great cost..."

dialogue.content: "Borrowed?" Chen Ji's voice trembled, "What do you mean? She's not my biological sister?" The phantom's form had become almost transparent, she used her last strength to say: "She is... a wisp of split soul reincarnation from me... ten thousand years ago... I need her inside the Holy Sect... to counter the Heavenly Eye's scheme... Ji'er, the drama of sisters turning against each other... is precisely what the Heavenly Eye fears most..." The light specks began to dissipate. "Mother... gives you one final piece of advice... the more complete the Tianji Record... the stronger the backlash... remember... remember..."

choices.description: For ten thousand years, she chose to hide in the shadows scheming rather than accompany my growth

text.content: "I only want to ask one thing." Chen Ji suddenly spoke, his voice terrifyingly calm, "Since you could scheme for ten thousand years, since you could deceive the Heavenly Eye—why couldn't you deceive it to accompany me?" The phantom froze. "Even just one day." Chen Ji's voice finally cracked, "Even if only holding me once, telling me I'm not a jinx, not a disaster, not... a waste rejected by everyone."

dialogue.content: The phantom's figure convulsed violently, crystal tears sliding from her eyes, yet evaporating into nothingness before they could fall. "Ji'er..." her voice shattered beyond recognition, "It's not that I didn't want to... I couldn't... the Heavenly Eye constantly monitors everyone connected to the Tianji Record... if I approached you... it would sense me immediately... that high fever when you were seven that nearly killed you... I used a secret technique to shield you from that tribulation... Mother has always been here..." Her form began to dissipate rapidly. "I'm sorry... Ji'er... I'm sorry..."

text.content: The light specks vanished completely, leaving only the surging golden runes and the silent Chen Ji standing motionless, as if his soul had been extracted. After a long while, he slowly reached out his hand, gently stroking the cover of the Tianji Record, his fingertips trembling slightly. "So that's how it was." His voice was hoarse, as if squeezed from the depths of his throat, "So Mother was watching over me all along."

Tears finally slipped from the corners of Chen Ji's eyes, but he ruthlessly wiped them away. He closed his eyes, took a deep breath, and when he opened them again, those pupils had regained their usual composure and depth. "The Heavenly Eye..." he murmured to himself, a cold arc curving at the corner of his lips, "So you've been searching for me all along. I thought I was just a捡来的残页— a stray fragment someone picked up, but I never imagined... from the very beginning, I was the prey." He opened the Tianji Record, gazing at the text slowly emerging on the blank page— that was the last piece of information his mother left: The Ancient Forbidden Land, where the core of the Heavenly Eye lies, and where Chen Nian is trapped.

Chen Ji closed the Tianji Record, his eyes gleaming with sharp light. He recalled what Mo Xiansheng had said— "Complete each scroll's objective to unseal a page of knowledge." The first scroll's objective was to survive the Sect Competition, and he succeeded; the second scroll's objective was to enter the Ancient Forbidden Land... his gaze shifted, deep in thought. "It seems it's time to quicken my pace." He gazed out the window, where dawn's first light was beginning to spread across the horizon. "Mother, you schemed for ten thousand years just to have me end all of this—" he said softly, "Then your son shall fulfill your wish."
